title: Income Annuities Installments Held in Suspense When a Death Is Confirmed: Release and Forfeiture
content:
Once the death that ended the suspension of an Ashgrove Income Annuities contract is confirmed, an installment still held in suspense for a payment date after the death is settled in one step: the share owed to a living payee is released to that payee by the payment method on the contract and the rest is forfeited back to the contract, the held installment earning no interest, and no part of a held installment is ever counted as an overpayment.

## Standing conditions

The survivor share of a held installment is fixed only after every installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death carries a repayment entry for its excess.

A held installment that fell due after the first death is not released until every installment held for a payment date on or before that death stands released.

Restated in the same terms, as the activity history shows them:

- while any installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death has no repayment entry for its excess, the survivor share of a held installment is not yet fixed;
- while any installment held for a payment date on or before the first death does not stand released, no held installment that fell due after the first death is released.

## Settlement in one step

| Part of the held installment | Goes to |
|---|---|
| The share owed to a living payee | Released to that payee, by the payment method on the contract |
| The rest | Forfeited back to the contract |
| Interest on the held installment | None is earned |
| Overpayment | No part of a held installment is ever counted as an overpayment |

**Effect.** The activity history shows, for the held payment date, a forfeited part and a released part, the paid installment with its gross amount and the amount actually sent, and — where part of the share is applied to an overpayment still owed — a recovery linked to the deposit it came from; the balance held in suspense, the unreturned purchase amount and the overpayment owed fall accordingly.

## Settling the held installment: `release_survivor_share_80ea435e`

**Capability.** Settles an installment held in suspense on an Ashgrove income annuity after the first death on a joint contract: releases the survivor's share to the surviving payee and forfeits the rest back to the contract, applying any part of the survivor's share that recovers an overpayment still owed. One call books the forfeited part and the released survivor share for the stated payment date, books the paid installment with its gross amount and the amount actually sent, books the recovery of the amount applied to the overpayment against the deposit it came from (none when that amount is zero), and lowers the contract's balance held in suspense, its unreturned purchase amount and its overpayment owed accordingly. The survivor sees the payment at once.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: unlock it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then call it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `income_contract_id` | Reference number of the income annuity contract holding the installment, from the income annuity contract lookup | Identifier as recorded |
| `payment_due_date` | Scheduled payment date of the held installment, as shown on its held entry | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `payee_name` | The survivor's full name exactly as the customer profile lookup shows it | Verbatim, character for character |
| `payment_method` | How the money is sent | `direct_deposit` (to the deposit account on the contract's payment instructions) or `check` (a paper check mailed to the mailing address on the contract) |
| `gross_amount` | The gross survivor share released, before any withholding or recovery | USD, 2 decimal places |
| `forfeited_amount` | The part of the held installment forfeited back to the contract | USD, 2 decimal places |
| `offset_amount` | The part of the survivor share applied to an overpayment still owed on the contract | USD, 2 decimal places; 0.00 when none is applied |
| `offset_source_txn_id` | Reference number of the deposit whose overpayment the applied amount recovers, as shown on its entry in the activity history | Identifier as recorded; empty string when nothing is applied |
| `net_paid_amount` | The amount actually sent after federal and state tax withholding and after the amount applied to the overpayment | USD, 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A receipt line beginning "Released" with the gross share and the payment date held, the contract, the amount forfeited and the amount applied to the overpayment, the reference numbers of the forfeiture, release and paid installment entries, and the net amount sent in USD with 2 decimal places. A receipt beginning "Released" means the entries are booked.
